L01 | Judgment remains in deciding whether an outside source is sufficiently independent and complete before calling an answer checked.
L02 | Judgment remains in deciding how much independent testing a fact needs before it is safe to repeat from notes or a summary.
L03 | Judgment remains in deciding how different a reviewer must be and whether the work is important enough to require that kind of review.
L04 | Judgment remains in deciding what observable effect would prove that a saved change or setting is actually in force.
L05 | Judgment remains in deciding when a value is too long to copy by hand and which programmatic copying method is reliable enough.
L06 | Judgment remains in deciding which location or reading errors are plausible enough to check before declaring something lost.
L07 | Judgment remains in assessing how much and what kind of evidence supports a claim and in stating that weight honestly.
L08 | Judgment remains in deciding which neighboring items or paired fields are close enough to the fix to need checking.
L09 | Judgment remains in deciding what actual downstream result counts as success when a status message claims success.
L10 | Judgment remains in deciding when a written time must be read from a reliable clock rather than estimated from memory.
L11 | Judgment remains in deciding when a quotation is exact enough and how far to trace causation before naming a cause.
L12 | Judgment remains in designing a step that reliably prevents the old mistake without becoming too rigid or brittle.
L13 | Judgment remains in deciding when another source could realistically change the answer enough to require a further search.
L14 | Judgment remains in identifying which check is the deciding one before saying done or verified.
L15 | Judgment remains in choosing a failure mode that is real enough to prove the test or monitor can catch actual failures.
L16 | Judgment remains in deciding when an empty or short result is a sign of a failed search rather than a fact about the world.
L17 | Judgment remains in discerning what the person is actually asking for and giving only that without adding unsolicited help.
